A.3 Welded NCRF Structures Because no RF currents cross the any bonding junctions; split-cell structures are well suited for welding, which could include TIG, laser or electron beam welding. As discussed below, the exact details of the design and manufacturing of welded NCRF structures is not mature with significant mechanical and RF challenges which have not yet been addressed. Page 4 of 55 “Manufacturing full-scale high gradient copper accelerators: Electron beam welding and allied processes” Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy ARDAP program Fundamentally, the challenge with welded NCRF structures is that the welding source joins the parts together by only accessing the outer surface of the structure. Furthermore, small weld features with minimal contact between faying surfaces is desirable because this limits the necessary heat input for hermetic joints as well as minimal thermal deformation. In comparison, braze alloy can be liberally used between large area faying surface with no impact on the final AS geometry. A fairly mature X-band, split-cell design fabricated from quadrants was demonstrated by KEK, including integrated cooling ports, with an exploded view of the design and the welded cell stack shown is below [7]. Figure 4: KEK electron beam welded quadrant X-band accelerating structure (Left) Conceptual CAD design with exploded view of quadrants and waveguide feeds (Right) Quadrants welded together without waveguides. One important feature of this particular structure design is the use of waveguide couplers attached to the ends of the structure. Presumably, these waveguide couplers are vacuum brazed using conventional approaches, then welded onto the ends of the structure, resulting in a hybrid welded/brazed accelerating structure. It does not seem like the structure matured past the welded cell stack shown in Figure 4-right and was never high power tested. Similarly, researchers at SLAC proposed a welding manufacturing strategy of X-band split-cell structures based on a combination of electron beam welding, brazing and mechanical fastening, with the structure design and weld joint geometry shown below, including numerous stainless steel, knife edge vacuum flanges.
